readme.text:
| :warning: On September 1, 2021, Adobe will end support for Brackets. If you would like to continue using, maintaining, and improving Brackets, you may fork the project on [GitHub](https://github.com/adobe/brackets). Through Adobe’s partnership with Microsoft, we encourage users to migrate to [Visual Studio Code](https://aka.ms/brackets-to-vscode), Microsoft’s free code editor built on open source.
| ---

Welcome to Brackets!
-------------------

Brackets is a modern open-source code editor for HTML, CSS
and JavaScript that's *built* in HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

What makes Brackets different from other web code editors?

* **Tools shouldn't get in your way.** Instead of cluttering up your coding
environment with lots of panels and icons, the Quick Edit UI in Brackets puts
context-specific code and tools inline.
* **Brackets is in sync with your browser.** With Live Preview, Brackets
works directly with your browser to push code edits instantly and jump
back and forth between your real source code and the browser view.
* **Do it yourself.** Because Brackets is open source, and built with HTML, CSS
and JavaScript, you can [help build](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) the best code editor for the web.

Brackets may have reached version 1, but we're not stopping there. We have many feature ideas on our
[trello board](http://bit.ly/BracketsTrelloBoard) that we're anxious to add and other
innovative web development workflows that we're planning to build into Brackets.
So take Brackets out for a spin and let us know how we can make it your favorite editor.

You can see some
[screenshots of Brackets](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/Brackets-Screenshots)
on the wiki, [intro videos](http://www.youtube.com/user/CodeBrackets) on YouTube, and news on the [Brackets blog](http://blog.brackets.io/).

How to install and run Brackets
-------------------------------
#### Download

Installers for the latest stable build for Mac, Windows and Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) can be [downloaded here](http://brackets.io/).

#### Usage

By default, Brackets opens a folder containing some simple "Getting Started" content.
You can choose a different folder to edit using *File > Open Folder*.

Most of Brackets should be pretty self-explanatory, but for information on how
to use its unique features, like Quick Edit and Live Preview, please read
[How to Use Brackets](http://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/How-to-Use-Brackets).
Also, see the [release notes](http://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/Release-Notes)
for a list of new features and known issues in each build.

In addition to the core features built into Brackets, there is a large and growing
community of developers building extensions that add all sorts of useful functionality.
See the [Brackets Extension Registry](https://registry.brackets.io/)
for a list of available extensions. For installation instructions,
see the [extensions wiki page](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/Brackets-Extensions).

#### Need help?

Having problems starting Brackets the first time, or not sure how to use Brackets? Please
review [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/Troubleshooting), which helps
you to fix common problems and find extra help if needed.

Helping Brackets
----------------

#### I found a bug!

If you found a repeatable bug, and [troubleshooting](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/Troubleshooting)
tips didn't help, then be sure to [search existing issues](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/issues) first.
Include steps to consistently reproduce the problem, actual vs. expected results, screenshots, and your OS and
Brackets version number. Disable all extensions to verify the issue is a core Brackets bug.
[Read more guidelines for filing good bugs.](https://github.com/adobe/brackets/wiki/How-to-Report-an-Issue)

#### I have a new suggestion, but don't know how to program!

For feature requests please first check our [Trello board](http://bit.ly/BracketsBacklog) to
see if it's already there; you can upvote it if so. If not, feel free to file it as an issue as above; we'll
move it to the feature backlog for you.

#### I want to help with the code!…

causeOfDeath.headline: Official corporate euthanasia in favor of Microsoft Visual Studio Code
causeOfDeath.explanation: Adobe explicitly sunset Brackets on September 1, 2021, encouraging its user base to migrate to VS Code. The commit history shows automated localization updates and minor fixes leading up to commit f0cae55 ('EOL Notification (#15325)').

timeOfDeath.note: Commit f0cae55 officially added the EOL Notification notice to the repository.

diagnosis.evidence: VS Code dominated the web-built text editor landscape, prompting Adobe to explicitly direct users to migrate to VS Code in the README.
Built on custom CEF/Node shells during the early 2010s HTML/JS desktop app era, it lost ecosystem velocity compared to Electron-standardized platforms.
The last commits in early 2020 and 2021 were mostly automated localization updates ('Updated by ALF automation') and minor path fixes before the final EOL notice.

worthSaving: Inline Quick Edit UI pattern for context-sensitive CSS/JS editing
Extensive history of web-centric editor extension architecture

marketToday.reasoning: The web-editor landscape is firmly dominated by VS Code, modern web-based IDEs, and AI-native editors like Cursor. Rebuilding an HTML/CSS/JS text editor from 2011 without deep AI integration or modern language server protocol native support offers no competitive edge today.

autopsy.revivalScoreReason: The owner officially archived the project and surrendered the market to VS Code, leaving thousands of abandoned open issues.
autopsy.epitaph: Pioneered web editors in HTML, only to be retired by VS Code.

resurrection.honestNote: Brackets as a general-purpose web editor is dead; VS Code and Cursor own that market completely. The revival strategy pivots the original inline Quick Edit UI into a lightweight browser extension that brings instant, context-aware visual CSS/HTML tweaking directly into production sites for freelance designers.

newPositioning.oneLiner: Inline visual CSS editing inside your live browser tab.
newPositioning.targetUser: Freelance web designers editing client sites on Webflow or WordPress
newPositioning.painPoint: Constantly context-switching between DevTools and source files to tweak UI spacing and fonts.
newPositioning.whyNow: Chrome Extension Manifest V3 and modern DOM mutation APIs make zero-latency overlay editing effortless without a heavy desktop IDE.

keep: Inline Quick Edit UI panel over target HTML elements
Live CSS rule inspection and direct manipulation
Instant export of modified styles as clean CSS snippets
kill: Desktop file system access — because we run entirely as a Chrome extension
Custom extension registry — because standard browser extension APIs handle storage
Node/CEF desktop runtime wrapper — because native browser DOM is faster
Built-in web server — because we inject directly into live pages
build: One-click CSS copy/export for applied page changes

crowdfundingPitch.title: Brackets Inline Quick Edit — Relaounced as a Chrome Extension
crowdfundingPitch.story: I used to love Adobe Brackets for its unique inline editing UI. But when Adobe officially sunset the project in 2021 to steer everyone toward VS Code, the core idea of friction-free contextual editing got lost inside massive desktop editors. General-purpose code editors lost the simple magic of quick web tweaking. I decided to resurrect Brackets' best feature—the Quick Edit overlay—and bring it straight into modern browser tabs. No heavy desktop runtimes, no complex build setups. Just instant visual style editing for freelance designers working directly on live web pages.
fundingUse: Chrome Web Store developer registration and publishing pipeline setup
Cross-browser compatibility testing across Chrome, Edge, and Brave
Hosting for public docs and export template hosting
crowdfundingPitch.backerReward: Get early access to private beta builds and get your name listed as a founding backer in the extension options menu.

resurrection.aiBuildPrompt: Build a Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) using React and Tailwind CSS that injects an inline CSS editor panel onto any web page. Target user: Freelance web designers. Primary feature: User clicks an element on the active page, a floating UI panel appears floating next to the element (inspired by Brackets Quick Edit). The panel shows controls for font-size, line-height, color, margin, and padding. Changing inputs updates the element's styles in real-time. Include a 'Copy Diff' button in the toolbar that generates valid CSS code for all modified elements on the page. Do NOT build a file tree, desktop integration, or code editor tab. Definition of done: Extension loads via Chrome Developer Mode, permits selecting DOM nodes on any site, updates styles instantly, and copies changed CSS rules to clipboard.
